value.reason: The Evidence shows the same pattern as the positive example. server.ts:362-369 sets up a daily rotating access log stream (logs/access.log.%DATE%) with max_logs: '2d', so access logs are deleted after 2 days. server.ts:370 sends Morgan 'combined' output to that stream, and this format records the full request URL, including the query string. frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:54-55 sends the current, new and repeat passwords as query parameters in a GET to /rest/user/change-password. Those authentication secrets therefore end up in the access logs, which is sensitive information written to a log file. Keeping traffic and processing logs for only 2 days also falls well short of the one-year minimum in DPDP Rule 6(1)(e), which requires logs for detecting and investigating unauthorised access, and Rule 8(3), which requires keeping associated traffic data and logs. Both problems are real: the short retention breaks the logging rules, and the credentials should not be in the URL or the logs at all.
